about: I am the founder of Synora, a provider-agnostic AI orchestration platform, and VRIKSHAM, an agroforestry and carbon-finance model for smallholder farmers.

about: My work sits where system architecture meets verification: how multi-model AI should be structured, how AI-assisted engineering should report what is actually proven, and how to decide early whether a new technology is worth building at all.
about: I am self-taught in AI systems, financial modelling and carbon-market methodology, and I am pursuing an MBA in FinTech with AI. I work in English and Hindi.

id: vriksham-error
title: Catching a 100× error in my own carbon model
tag: VRIKSHAM · Financial modelling
status: Pre-pilot · projections, not results
tone: plan
problem: An early version of the VRIKSHAM financial model overstated carbon income by about 100 times, which made the idea look far stronger than it was.
action[0]: Rebuilt the model with timber as the main income and carbon credits as a secondary stream.
action[1]: Counted only net credits: after a 20% buffer and 15% leakage deduction, 30 gross credits become 20.4 net credits per farmer per year.
action[2]: Limited the platform fee (35%) to carbon income, and left timber income entirely with the farmer.
action[3]: Stress-tested a nine-year model, and marked the timber price as still needing local verification.
outcome: Working projection: about ₹8.86 lakh per farmer over seven years, of which carbon is ₹0.23 lakh (roughly 3%). The corrected model is smaller and more credible, and the earlier plan is marked as superseded.
lesson: A number that looks exciting is a reason to derive it again from the assumptions.

id: gateway
title: One interface, many models: Synora's provider-agnostic gateway
tag: Synora · Architecture
status: MVP in a controlled pilot gate
tone: active
problem: Products built directly on one AI vendor inherit its pricing, outages and policy changes. Synora is meant to outlast any single provider.
action[0]: Designed a seven-layer system in which routing, tools and memory sit above interchangeable model providers.
action[1]: Put every provider behind an adapter that exposes one internal interface, so a vendor can be replaced without touching core logic.
action[2]: Served open-weight models (DeepSeek, NVIDIA Nemotron, Qwen) through one OpenAI-compatible gateway, with Redis short-term memory and PostgreSQL with pgvector.
outcome: In my own deployment (August 2026) these were tested: registration and login, conversation persistence, provider abstraction, cost controls and per-user limits, container health checks, auto-recovery after restart, HTTPS and security headers, and restore-tested backups. Of eight capabilities, one is active, one is available through an API, and six are not configured yet. Public launch is targeted for 2027.
lesson: Provider-specific behaviour stays behind adapters, so the core never depends on one vendor.

id: evidence-status
title: Never report “done” without evidence
tag: Synora · Engineering method
status: In use
tone: done
problem: AI-assisted engineering can produce confident reports of work that was never run or checked.
action[0]: Defined seven statuses (Implemented, Tested, Locally verified, Integration verified, Production verified, Not verified, Blocked), each needing its own evidence.
action[1]: Added a claim-classification scheme so facts, inferences and assumptions are not blended.
action[2]: Wrote Git safety and reconciliation procedures after resolving a conflict between parallel cloud and local agent workstreams.
outcome: Untested work is no longer reported as complete, and a missing credential is never turned into a claim that an integration works.
lesson: Implemented does not mean verified.

id: audit-own-reports
title: Auditing my own policy reports
tag: Public-interest research · Source checking
status: Corrected editions published here · 6 Nov 2026
tone: done
problem: My July 2026 governance drafts contained figures I could not trace and some that official data contradicted.
action[0]: Checked each figure against a source, and removed anything I could not trace instead of estimating it.
action[1]: Undertrial prisoners: the draft said 40–45%, but NCRB reports 75.8% (4,34,302 of 5,73,220) at the end of 2022.
action[2]: PMKVY: the draft said “94.53% fake beneficiaries”, but the CAG finding was that bank details were missing or invalid in over 94% of records (9.06 million of 9.59 million). That is a data-quality finding, not a count of fake people.
action[3]: Learning outcomes: the draft claimed a steady decline, but ASER 2024 shows recovery, with Std III reading at 23.4% against 16.3% in 2022.
outcome: Thirteen corrected governance documents and four VRIKSHAM documents, each with a table of sourced figures, a source list and a record of what changed. Several sources are news reports of official data, and replacing them with the primary publications is the next step.
lesson: Check your own work first, and publish the corrections.

id: rscp
title: Validating a problem before building the product
tag: RSCP · Hardware research
status: Feasibility complete · Aug 2026
tone: done
problem: When one part fails in a tightly integrated device, user data can become unreachable even though it is physically intact.
action[0]: Visited repair shops to check that the problem is real for people who deal with it.
action[1]: Led a 38-page feasibility assessment.
action[2]: Narrowed the scope to data survival across hardware replacement.
outcome: A smaller, testable scope, ready for an informed decision on whether to proceed.
lesson: Narrow the problem until it can be tested.

id: aura
title: A research gate that is allowed to say no
tag: Project AURA · Decision research
status: Research · since Aug 2026
tone: active
problem: Should a new AI-native programming paradigm be built at all?
action[0]: Ran a prior-art analysis, and set a four-outcome gate in advance: No-Go, Conditional Go, Go, or Research-Contribution Go.
action[1]: Kept an append-only decision log.
outcome: Phase 1 leaned No-Go on a general-purpose language, and flagged independent benchmarking of AI-native languages as an open problem.
lesson: Decide what would count as a No-Go before falling in love with the idea.
